To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cAMP-dependent protein kinases phosphorylate a 27-kDa protein, the major protein component of liver gap junction channels, and that phosphorylation of this gap junction protein increases the conductance of the channels.
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation increases the conductance of the gap junction and that this effect occurs by increasing the open probability of the channel.
cAMP-dependent protein kinases increase gap junction permeability by phosphorylation of the junctional polypeptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the 27 kDa major gap junction protein in the modulation of liver gap junction conductance and permeability.
the role of the gap junction in the control of intercellular communication.
the regulation of gap junctional conductances and the role of phosphorylation of gap junction polypeptides in the regulation of gap-junctional communication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 27 kDa protein, which forms the gap junction channel, is phosphorylated by the catalytic subunits of cAMP-dependent kinase.
the cAMP-dependent phosphorylating system of the gap junction is a major regulatory mechanism of liver gap junctional conductances.
phosphorylation of gap junction protein by a cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation system is involved in regulation of the conductance of gap junction channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation of gap junction channels regulates the conductance of gap junctions.
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation modulates the conductances of the gap junctional channels.
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation modulates the conductances of gap junctions in hepatocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation is an important mechanism for modulating gap junctional conductances in liver.
cAMP-dependent protein phosphorylation is a major regulatory mechanism of gap junction channels in liver.
gap junctions are modifiable. They can change their permeability and their conductance.
